title: HTTP /environments/read serves the required-vs-set table, composed into the production listener
description:
PREREQUISITE row filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-05 while planning task-ba83b202265d40d1885d3091f009b0a2 (the Environments screen), which cannot read anything without it. That row now declares dependsOn against this one.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04):
- `ls apps/daemon/src/http/ | grep -i env` returns NOTHING. No environments route exists.
- `grep -n design apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` and the equivalent for environments return nothing either.
- Child 1 task-d0c63cd8848a4da18ad3fbb8eb1d95c3 is DONE, and its own completionSummary states the scope precisely: "17 paths, all new, all under apps/daemon/src/environment/. Nothing outside that directory changed." Its "reads" are IN-PROCESS projection functions - `readEnvironmentState` (:80), `projectEnvironmentVariables` (:95), `EnvironmentReadOk` (:49), `EnvironmentReadResult` (:61) in apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-projection.ts - not an HTTP surface.
So the store and the projection exist and are DONE; the operator-facing READ does not. This row closes exactly that gap, symbol by symbol, rather than letting the screen row invent a daemon route it does not own or mock one in a test.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: `/environments/read` serving, per environment, the variable table as {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} and NO VALUE - plus its composition into the PRODUCTION listener, in the SAME row. Do not repeat the design-read split: task-7ca9dca3 served /design/read and task-eb2bb09d then had to exist purely to compose the port into the listener, because a served route nothing mounts satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

THE PATTERN TO FOLLOW is apps/daemon/src/http/design-read.ts (with its .js bridge and design-read.test.ts), composed through apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, http-listener.ts, http-listener-guards.ts and apps/daemon/src/daemon-entry.ts. Read all five before writing; the guard and dispatch seams are where a route silently fails to mount.

A VALUE MUST NEVER CROSS THIS BOUNDARY. The projection already returns no value; this row must not add one back in a response field, an error body, a log line or a trace. That is epic rail 3 and it is the reason this route exists as its own row rather than as a field bolted onto an existing read.
definitionOfDone: `/environments/read` serves, per environment, a variable table of {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} built from the EXISTING projection in apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-projection.ts (`readEnvironmentState`, `projectEnvironmentVariables`). It reimplements no store logic - assert the reuse with a grep in the completion record.

NO VALUE CROSSES THE BOUNDARY, asserted as its own arm and not merely by inspection: seed a variable with a known distinctive value, call the route, and assert that value appears NOWHERE in the response body, in any error body, or in any log line the request emits. Repeat for the refusal paths. This is epic rail 3 and it is the whole reason the route is a separate row.

THE ROUTE IS COMPOSED INTO THE PRODUCTION LISTENER IN THIS SAME ROW - http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, http-listener.ts / http-listener-guards.ts and daemon-entry.ts as the design-read precedent requires. Assert it is reachable from the composed production listener, not only from a hand-built test server. A served route nothing mounts satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist; that is exactly why task-eb2bb09d had to exist after task-7ca9dca3.
The response decoder contract is EXACT-KEY: an unknown key and a missing key each refuse, asserted with the specific code AND the layer that refused, never merely that it failed.

ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN is asserted with code AND layer for an unknown environment, reusing child 1's already-closed code->layer map rather than minting a second one. Reuse an already-rostered layer literal; introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line as evidence.
taskRails: A VALUE NEVER CROSSES THIS BOUNDARY - not in a response field, not in an error body, not in a log line, not in a trace, not in a committed fixture.
SERVE AND COMPOSE IN THE SAME ROW. A route that is served but not mounted is the failure that forced task-eb2bb09d to exist after task-7ca9dca3.
REUSE the existing projection (apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-projection.ts) and child 1's closed code->layer map. A second store path or a second refusal map is a rejection.
NO UI, NO PROXY PIN, NO CLIENT DECODER: the control-room half belongs to task-ba83b202265d40d1885d3091f009b0a2 and touching apps/control-room here collides in the shared worktree.

implementationPlan.description: THE ROUTE. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/http/environments-read.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (design-read.js sits beside design-read.ts; a missing bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Mirror `design-read.ts` (102 lines) structurally — read it first, it is the whole pattern in one file: a `*_READ_PATH` const, a `LAYER` const, a frozen codes roster, a refused() helper, an exact-key body decoder, a `*Dispatch` union with `REPLY` and `LISTENER_REFUSAL` arms, and a `handle*Request(dependencies, request)` that authenticates, checks a capability, then delegates to an injected PORT. NOTE THE SHAPE THAT KEEPS THIS TESTABLE: `DesignReadPort` is documented "Closed over a store by tests and by the composition sibling; this module does not open one." Do the same — no store handle here. THE BODY DECODER IS EXACT-KEY (DoD-4) and `designReadBodyOf` is the model, including the detail that matters: it rejects a `version` that is not a finite SAFE INTEGER so "a 1.5 cannot masquerade as ABSENT". Decide your own key set and enforce it by exact arity — an unknown key and a missing key each refuse. `projectId` comes from the AUTHENTICATED PRINCIPAL, never from the payload; design-read's header states that a payload naming it is an unknown key, and the same rule applies here. REUSE, DO NOT MINT: build the table from `readEnvironmentState` / `projectEnvironmentVariables`, and take `ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN` and its layer from child 1's closed map (DoD-5). INTRODUCE NO NEW `*_LAYER` CONSTANT — rail 5 — because a new layer literal demands a boundary-roster backfill this row does not own. The response carries {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} PER VARIABLE and NO VALUE; the projection already returns none, so the job here is not to add one back.
implementationPlan.note:
THE ROUTE. `apps/daemon/src/http/environments-read.ts` (130 lines, under the 250 cap) plus its one-line `.js` bridge, both NEW and UNTRACKED. Structurally mirrors design-read.ts: path const, frozen codes roster, `refused()` helper, exact-key decoder, `*Dispatch` union with REPLY / LISTENER_REFUSAL arms, `handle*Request(dependencies, request)` that authenticates, checks a capability, then delegates to an injected port. No store handle, no credential, no logging in the module.

REUSE (DoD-1, task rail 3). The port type is `EnvironmentsReadPort { read(input: {environment: string}): EnvironmentReadResult }`. `EnvironmentReadResult` is IMPORTED from `../environment/environment-store.js` — child 1's type, not a restatement. The composition sibling (step 3) will bind `read` to `readEnvironmentVariables`, which is child 1's own composition of `admitEnvironment` -> `answerEnvironmentRead` -> `readEnvironmentState` + `projectEnvironmentVariables`. This module derives no table, opens no seal, resolves no credential and never touches `environment-projection.ts` directly; there is no second store path to reimplement.

`environment` STAYS A RAW STRING on the way in — deliberately NOT validated here. A local `isEnvironmentName` check would be a SECOND scope authority and would answer before `ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN` could, making DoD-5's arm assert the wrong layer's refusal. That is exactly the "one added layer away from vacuous" failure global rail 1 names. The store is the only scope authority.

EXACT-KEY DECODER (DoD-4). `environmentsReadBodyOf` requires `Object.keys(record).length === 1 && keys[0] === "environment"`, then a non-empty string. Exact ARITY, so a MISSING key (`{}`, arity 0) and an UNKNOWN key (`{environment, projectId}`, arity 2) both fall to the same `null` and both become `LISTENER_ENVIRONMENTS_REQUEST_INVALID`. Chose arity over a "read the keys I know" decode precisely because the latter accepts `{environment, projectId}` and lets a caller believe it named a project it does not hold. projectId is never read from the payload; the principal is the only project authority.

NO NEW LAYER LITERAL (rail 5, DoD-5). I did NOT copy design-read.ts:14's module-local `LAYER = "DESIGN_READ"`. `ENVIRONMENTS_READ_CAPABILITY_DENIED` carries `CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER_LAYER` ("CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER", http-listener-guards.ts:16) — already rostered, already what every `refuseRequest` on this listener writes, typed as `typeof CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER_LAYER` so a string cannot drift in. Every `ENV_*` refusal arrives from the store already paired with its layer by the closed `ENVIRONMENT_CODE_LAYERS` map; this module mints none of them and adds no second map.

CAPABILITY IS ADMIN, NOT GOAL. design-read uses `CAPABILITIES.GOAL`; a variable table is deployment-secret metadata, so `CAPABILITIES.ADMIN` — the capability that installs policy — is the honest fence. Recorded here because it is a deliberate divergence from the pattern the plan told me to mirror.

NO VALUE (DoD-2, epic rail 3). The port answer is forwarded VERBATIM at 200; the module reshapes nothing, so there is no field for a value to be assembled into. Refusal bodies are the store's own frozen prose (`ENVIRONMENT_REFUSAL_DETAILS`, never interpolated) or `{code, layer, outcome}`. Nothing in this file logs, traces or stringifies the request or the answer.

The two `LISTENER_ENVIRONMENTS_*` codes are declared in the Dispatch union here but are not yet rostered in `http-listener-guards.ts`, so `ListenerRefusalCode` does not admit them and typecheck will red until step 3 lands the roster and `statusFor` entries. Deliberately deferred to the composition step rather than split across two files mid-write; no gate quoted for this step.

implementationPlan.description: TESTS, WITH THE NO-VALUE ARM AS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/http/environments-read.test.ts`, modelled on `design-read.test.ts`. (1) DoD-2, THE ROW'S REASON FOR EXISTING, and it must be hostile rather than confirmatory: seed a variable with a DISTINCTIVE known value, call the route, and assert that value appears NOWHERE — not in the success body, not in any refusal body, not in any log line the request emits. Serialize the whole response and grep it for the value rather than checking named fields, because a field-by-field check passes while the value rides in a field you did not think to name. REPEAT FOR THE REFUSAL PATHS: an unknown environment, a capability denial, a malformed body. The refusal paths are where a value leaks in practice, because an error message is where someone reaches for context. (2) DoD-4: exact-key decoding — an unknown key refuses, a missing key refuses, each asserted with the CODE and the LAYER, never merely that it failed. (3) DoD-5: `ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN` with code AND layer for an unknown environment, and assert the layer is one already on the roster — not a new literal. (4) DoD-1: the table is built from the existing projection — assert the served shape matches what `projectEnvironmentVariables` produces for the same seeded state, so a reimplementation would diverge and red. (5) DoD-3, THE REACHABILITY ARM: assert the route answers from the COMPOSED PRODUCTION listener, not a hand-built server. `daemon-entry-ops.test.ts:139-174` is the precedent — it starts the entry with a provider and POSTs `/design/read`. Add the equivalent there, and also cover the factories-roster pin at :183-202 if the new key needs a line: that test asserts a FACTORY is accepted and a bare PORT is rejected, so a provider entry supplied as a value rather than a function fails there and nowhere else.
implementationPlan.note:
TESTS. 24 new arms across 3 files. `apps/daemon/src/http/environments-read.test.ts` is NEW (19 arms); 4 arms added to `daemon-entry-ops.test.ts`; 1 to `daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts`.

(1) DoD-2, THE NO-VALUE PROPERTY, written hostile. Canary `SECRET = "zzq-PLAINTEXT-CANARY-vvx-9137-must-never-appear"` — deliberately NOT hex, so it can never be confused with the sha256 fingerprint the route IS allowed to publish. Every no-value arm `JSON.stringify`s the WHOLE dispatch result and searches the text; none checks a named field, because a field-by-field check passes while the value rides in a field the test never thought to name. `withCapturedLog` spies all six console sinks (debug/error/info/log/trace/warn) around the call and joins what was written, so a route that keeps the value out of the body by logging it fails here.
  - success path: 1 arm.
  - REFUSAL paths: 4 cases via `it.each` — unknown environment, unknown key, missing key, non-string environment — plus a separate capability-denial arm. These are the ones the step calls "where a value leaks in practice".
  - NOT VACUOUS, two ways: the seed asserts `seeded.ok === true` (a sweep over an empty table would find no value and pass while proving nothing); and each arm carries a positive control — the success arm asserts the payload really does contain `DATABASE_URL` and that `` `${serialized}${SECRET}` `` DOES contain the canary, proving the search would have found it; the refusal arms assert `not.toContain("\"ok\":true")`, proving the request really was refused.

DoD-3's FILE LIST WOULD LEAD A WORKER STRAIGHT INTO THE FAILURE THIS ROW WAS FILED TO PREVENT. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 8 files (2 new).

The row is right that serve-and-compose must be one row. But its composition list is incomplete and partly wrong, and following it literally produces exactly the task-eb2bb09d outcome.

## The measured chain is SEVEN sites, not four

`git grep -n 'design-read|designRead|DESIGN_READ_PATH' -- apps/daemon/src`:

| site | what |
|---|---|
| `http/design-read.ts` + `.js` bridge + test | the route |
| `http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` | **five** points: import :36, PATH roster :88-93, dependency pass :368, method guard :480, dispatch branch :554 |
| `http-listener.ts:158` | optional port on the deps interface |
| `daemon-entry-port-resolution.ts` | **five** points incl. a KEY ROSTER at :151 |
| **`daemon-store-dependencies.ts:119`** | **production provider factory — NOT in DoD-3** |
| **`daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:344`/:504** | **port built over the store — NOT in DoD-3** |
| `daemon-entry-ops.test.ts:139-174`, `:183-202` | reachability from the real entry, plus the factories-roster pin |

**Two corrections:** DoD-3 names `daemon-entry.ts`, but the file is `daemon-entry-port-resolution.ts`. And it omits the two files that *are* the production wiring — i.e. precisely what "composed into the PRODUCTION listener, not only from a hand-built test server" means.

Wire only the four named files and you get a route that answers in a test and does not exist in the product. **Drill (ii) is built to catch it:** remove only the `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` entry, leaving dispatch, listener and port resolution intact, and require the reachability arm to go red. If it stays green, that arm is testing a hand-built server and the row has not proven its own point.

**Third correction:** DoD-3 names `http-listener-guards.ts`, but the design-read trace shows **no guard site there** — the method guard lives in the dispatch file at :480. The plan tells the worker to say so rather than invent an edit to match the list.

## The provider entry must be a factory, not a port

`daemon-entry-ops.test.ts:183-202` pins `isDependencyProvider`: `designReads: () => port` passes, a bare `designReads: port` **fails**. Supplying a value reads correctly and fails only in that one test, far from the edit.

## The no-value arm has to be hostile, not confirmatory

Serialize the **whole** response and grep it for the seeded value — a field-by-field check passes while the value rides in a field nobody thought to name. And run it on the **refusal** paths too: an error message is where someone reaches for context, and it is where a value leaks in practice. Drill (i) makes the route echo the value and requires the arm to red with the leak visible.

## Smaller notes

`http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` (557) and `http-listener-guards.ts` (411) are **both already over the 400 cap at merge-base** — pre-existing, not this row's to fix, and not to be worsened. Add the branch, reformat nothing.

The PATH roster (:88-93) and the dispatch branch (:554) are two separate edits and either alone leaves a hole — drill (iii) covers the roster half.

One thing worth a conscious answer rather than silence: **the variable NAME is published even though the value is not**. That is the point of a required-vs-set table, but a name can itself be sensitive, and a sha256 fingerprint of a two-character value is closer to a disclosure than it looks. The adversarial pass asks for a stated conclusion.
